title: Company-wide policies and processes — master reference
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This document is the canonical, company-wide reference for core policies and operational processes used across Redwood Inference. It consolidates practices for access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel, and standard internal templates. Teams should follow the processes below and link back to this page from team-specific runbooks and onboarding guides.

Scope

- Applies to all full-time employees, contractors, and vendors with company network or data access.
- Covers corporate systems (G Suite/Workspace, Okta, internal services), cloud accounts, procurement under finance authority, and travel booked on behalf of the company.
- Excludes team-specific technical runbooks (those live in each team's confluence space).

Ownership and contact

- Primary owner: People Ops (people-ops@redwood-inference.com) — policy, role templates, offboarding coordination.
- Finance owner: Finance & Legal (finance@redwood-inference.com) — procurement thresholds, vendor contracts, expense policy enforcement.
- Security owner: Security & Compliance (security@redwood-inference.com) — access reviews, vendor security assessments, data handling guidance.

Principles (applies to all sections)

1. Principle of least privilege: grant the minimum set of permissions required for a job to be performed.
2. Role-based access: use role/group assignments rather than granting permissions to individuals where possible.
3. Auditability: all changes that affect production or access to sensitive data must be logged and periodically reviewed.
4. Clear ownership: every service, vendor, and procurement item must have an identified owner and approver.

1) Access and permissions

Summary

This section describes account provisioning, role templates, privileged access, periodic access review, and offboarding.

Provisioning (new hires and contractors)

- All new hires/contractors are onboarded through People Ops. Request process: people-ops ticket with role, start date, and manager.
- Standard role templates live in People Ops templates: Engineering, Product, Sales, Finance, Security, SRE. Managers must select the correct role template on the onboarding ticket.
- Time-to-provision target: 48 business hours for standard access; 5 business days for privileged (admin) access that requires security review.

Privileged access and approvals

- Admin-level access (Okta admin, cloud account owner, database superuser) requires:
  1) Justification from manager,
  2) Approval from Security, and
  3) Owner-level pairing for the first 14 days where applicable.
- Privileged access is granted for a defined duration and must be renewed if still required.

Periodic access reviews

- Teams must perform quarterly access reviews for all roles with production access. Security will run an automated monthly audit and flag anomalies.
- Review steps: confirm current list, revoke stale access, document exceptions with expiration.

Offboarding and access revocation

- Offboarding is triggered by People Ops. Standard offboarding checklist:
  1) Revoke SSO/Okta account immediately on termination OR at EOD for resignations with notice.
  2) Revoke cloud console and privileged API keys within 2 hours for terminated employees.
  3) Collect company assets and update asset register.
  4) Ensure code, docs, and owned services have new owners assigned.

2) Change management

Purpose

To ensure predictable, auditable changes to production systems while minimizing downtime and risk.

Change classifications

- Standard change: routine, low-risk (e.g., config tweak) — requires owner sign-off and a CI/CD link.
- Minor change: non-emergency, impacts services but with rollback plan — requires manager and SRE review.
- Major change: architectural or release windows that may impact multiple teams — requires Change Advisory Board (CAB) approval.
- Emergency change: response to an incident; must be documented post-facto in the incident ticket and reviewed by SRE.

Change process (numbered)

1. Submit a change request in the change board Jira project with: summary, owner, risk level, rollback plan, and deployment window.
2. For minor/major changes, schedule a pre-change review with SRE and at least one stakeholder.
3. CAB meets weekly; major changes must be submitted 5 business days before the desired window.
4. Post-deployment verification: owner confirms success and updates the change ticket within 24 hours.
5. Emergency changes require an after-action documentation within 72 hours.

Change windows and blackout periods

- Regular deploy window: Mon-Fri 02:00-06:00 UTC for low-impact infra changes.
- Blackout: end-of-quarter reporting windows and major marketing events; CAB publishes blackout calendar quarterly.

3) Data management

Classification

- Public: safe for public distribution.
- Internal: company confidential but not restricted.
- Restricted: PII, customer data, or regulated data (HIPAA/CCPA relevant).

Storage and handling

- Restricted data must be stored only in approved, encrypted systems (approved list maintained by Security).
- Use customer-specific VPCs or redaction flows for production data used in development.
- Backups: daily snapshots for core databases; retention policy is 90 days for standard, 365 days for audit-critical data unless otherwise approved by Legal.

Retention and deletion

- Default data retention: 3 years for Internal systems, 90 days for non-essential logs, unless regulated or covered by contractual obligations.
- Data deletion requests: submit to data-requests@redwood-inference.com with justification and retention evidence. Legal must approve deletion of regulated customer data.

Access to production data for dev/testing

- Production data must not be used in non-production environments without documented approval and masking. Masking techniques include tokenization, field redaction, and synthetic dataset generation.
- Any approved data export requires approval from Security and the data owner and must be logged.

4) Procurement and expenses

Procurement thresholds and approvals

- Low-value purchases (<= $500): team manager approval.
- Medium purchases ($501-$5,000): Finance approval required.
- Large purchases (> $5,000): Finance + Procurement team approval and vendor onboarding checklist.
- Capital equipment/long-term commitments: must be reviewed by Finance and Legal (contracts@redwood-inference.com).

Purchase process (step-by-step)

1. Create a purchase request in the procurement Jira board with business justification, budget code, and expected delivery date.
2. Finance checks budget availability and approves.
3. Procurement sends PO and manages vendor terms.
4. Goods received: confirm receipt in procurement ticket and route invoice for payment.

Corporate card and expense policy

- Company card holders must complete expense reports within 10 business days of travel or purchase.
- Allowed expenses: client meals (reason and attendees documented), airfare, lodging, ground transportation, reasonable meals and tips.
- Disallowed expenses: personal entertainment, family travel, fines, and illegal purchases.
- Per diem guidance: use company default per diem by region when expense receipts are not available.

Reimbursements and timelines

- Reimbursement processed within one payroll cycle after approval. Lost receipts require approver signoff on an expense attestation form.

5) Vendor management

Onboarding checklist

- Business case and owner assigned.
- Security questionnaire and risk classification (completed by Security).
- Contract review: Procurement + Legal.
- Data handling addendums (DPA) where required.
- Access provisioning limited to least privilege; reviewed quarterly.

Vendor risk levels and controls

- Low: SaaS with no access to restricted data — standard contract.
- Medium: vendors with access to internal data or developer tools — require SOC 2 or equivalent and quarterly review.
- High: vendors that process restricted customer data — require DPA, penetration test results, and executive sign-off.

Termination and exit strategy

- All vendor contracts must include data return/destruction clauses and a defined transition plan.
- Offboarding steps: revoke access, confirm data deletion/destruction, and perform post-mortem with owner and Security.

6) Travel policy

Booking and approvals

- Employees should use the company travel portal or preferred travel agency for business travel.
- Manager approval required for all travel. International travel requires pre-approval from People Ops for visas and additional safety checks.

Allowed expenses

- Flights: economy for <8h flights; premium economy may be approved for >8h with manager pre-approval.
- Lodging: mid-range business hotels; receipted room charges only.
- Ground transport: rideshare or rental cars as appropriate.

Safety and incident reporting

- Employees traveling for business must register travel dates and emergency contact with People Ops.
- Security incidents while traveling must be reported immediately to security@redwood-inference.com and People Ops.

7) Internal templates and artifacts

Quick links (templates)

- Onboarding role templates: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates
- Procurement request template: procurement Jira board template (link in procurement onboarding doc).
- Vendor security questionnaire: /confluence/security-and-compliance/vendor-security-questionnaire
- Travel reimbursement template: expense form in People Ops drive.

Standard forms available

- Access request form,
- Exception request form (for privileged access),
- Data deletion request form,
- Vendor onboarding checklist,
- Travel authorization form.

Process checklists (examples)

- Onboarding checklist (people-ops ticket): set up SSO, assign manager, set role groups, provision laptop, first-week 1:1 scheduling.
- Offboarding checklist: revoke accounts, transfer repos, disable tokens, collect assets.
- Procurement checklist: obtain 3 quotes for >$10k purchases, verify warranty/SLAs, record budget code.

Exceptions and escalation

- All exceptions must be documented via the exception request form and approved by the owning team and Security/Finance as appropriate. Exceptions are time-boxed and must have a documented mitigation plan.
- Escalation path: Team lead -> People Ops/Finance -> Security -> CTO for unresolved or high-risk items.

Revision history

- 2024-06-15: Initial consolidated policy authored by Aisha Patel.
- 2025-09-10: Major update to procurement thresholds and vendor risk levels.
- 2026-03-01: Quarterly refresh — clarified privileged access renewal and added backup retention specifics.

Appendix: contacts and resources

- People Ops: people-ops@redwood-inference.com
- Finance: finance@redwood-inference.com
- Security: security@redwood-inference.com
- Procurement: procurement@redwood-inference.com
- Legal/Contracts: contracts@redwood-inference.com

Related pages

- Team-specific runbooks and technical change procedures should link back to this page. Use the related_pages field above for cross-reference.

Amendments and review cadence

- This document will be reviewed at least annually by People Ops, Finance, and Security, and after any major incident that affects policy.
